title_en: Learn to Know Hours, Minutes, and Seconds
source_file: 教你认识时分秒（6-8 岁） .pptx
full_text_zh:
[P1] 我的第一本数学童话
教你认认时分秒
［韩］朴晓莹（박소영） 著
［意］芝拉·多拉（Cila Tortola） 绘
邓 楠 译
人民东方出版传媒
东方出版社

[P2] 太忙啦，太忙了！
恐龙先生是一位了不起的医生。它医术高明，治好了不少病人。上午8点恐龙医生去医院，它的手表一闪一闪的。

[P3] 上午10点
“医生，医生！我胸闷。”浣熊妈妈气喘吁吁地来找恐龙医生。恐龙医生拿出听器。“好，请慢慢呼吸。”“呼，呼，呼。是这样吗？”“不是的，不要这样，请3秒钟呼吸一次。”
3秒钟？

[P4] 恐龙医生伸出胳膊，给浣熊妈妈看手表。“您看好了，那根又细又长的针，‘滴答’动一下就是1秒。”浣熊妈妈点了点头。“啊，现在我明白了。”

给孩子看看代表“秒”的表针。
让孩子看到秒针运动的样子，听听秒针走动的声音。

滴答，滴答，滴答，呼。
滴答，滴答，滴答，呼。
3秒钟呼一气，胸闷的浣熊妈妈慢慢舒服了。

[P5] 下午2点
“医生，给我开点药吧！”“医生，给我打一针吧！”“我全身都疼！”恐龙医生忙得不可开交。
这时，“丁零零，丁零零”电话响了，是对面村子的犀牛爷爷。恐龙医生拿起电话说道：“现在我太忙了，请您1分钟之后再打过来吧。”

[P6] “1分钟？”犀牛爷爷问道。“秒针转一圈，就是1分钟。分针动一下也是1分钟。”“啊啊，那在心里数到60就是1分钟喽。”“当然喽，要是拍手拍60下也是1分钟。”“哈哈，现在知道什么是1分钟啦。”犀牛爷爷高兴地挂了电话。
让孩子看看钟表上的分针。如果直接让孩子看到秒针走一圈而分针走一格的话，印象会更深刻。

[P7] 下午4点
恐龙医生给肚子疼的小熊看病。“已经给你打过针了，很快就不疼了哦。饭后
30分钟一定记得吃药哦。”“饭后30分钟？”小熊困惑地摇摇头。

[P8] 恐龙医生给小熊看手表。
“分针转半圈的话就是30分钟。2个30分钟就是1个小时了。”

小熊笑眯眯地说：“要是我6点吃完饭的话，6点30分就该吃药了。”“嗯，就是这样的。”恐龙医生也微笑着说。

1个小时是60分钟。
那么2个30分钟就是1个小时。

[P9] 晚上7点
星星已经在眨眼了。恐龙医生开始换衣服准备回家了。
“嗯，路上大概需要1个小时，8点左右
我就能到家了。”

[P10] “咚咚咚！咚咚咚！”这时，不知是谁在敲门。原来是鸵鸟姐姐啊。
“医生，您快帮帮我。狗妈妈好像要生小狗了！”恐龙医生赶紧打开门。“快进来，来这边！”

[P11] 在恐龙医生帮助狗妈妈的时候，鸵鸟姐姐在一旁紧张地等待着。秒针滴答滴答，分针一格一格，时针一动不动，时间过得好慢啊。

[P12] 晚上9点
“恭喜你，可爱的小宝宝出生了。”听到恐龙医生的话，鸵鸟姐姐高兴地哭了。“恐龙医生，真是太感谢您了。”“哈哈哈，别客气。”
恐龙医生看着手表笑了，它度过了充实的一天，就像那一刻也不停的表针一样。

看着图画中的钟表，让孩子说一说几点。帮孩子算一算狗妈妈生小狗用了多长时间。

[P13] 拓展练习 来算一算时间吧。
要是不看钟表就能知道过了多少
时间该多好啊！用我自己的钟表来
算一下时间吧。
1秒钟
眼睛一闭一睁。
“啪”
拍一次手。
1分钟
健康成人心脏“扑
通扑通”跳60~100
次，也可以给小朋
友测量一下他们1
分钟的心跳次数。
和朋友
简单通话一次。
1个小时
看一个
有趣的电视节目。
画一幅漂亮的画并
涂上颜色。

[P14] 滴答滴答的钟表。
最短的表针表示“时”，一个小时是60分钟。
长长的表针是“分”，1分钟是60秒。
最细的表针表示“秒”。
表针是按这个方向运动的。
在钟表上画上表针。
30分钟之后，表针在哪儿呢？
1个小时之后，表针在哪儿呢？
2个小时之后，表针在哪儿呢？
full_text_en:
[P1] My First Math Fairy Tale
Teaching You to Recognize Hours, Minutes, and Seconds
[South Korea] Park So-young (박소영) Author
[Italy] Cila Tortola Illustrator
Deng Nan Translator
People's Oriental Publishing & Media
Oriental Press

[P2] So busy, so busy!
Mr. Dinosaur is a wonderful doctor. He is skilled and has cured many patients. At 8 a.m., Doctor Dinosaur goes to the hospital, and his watch flashes on and off.

[P3] 10:00 AM
"Doctor, doctor! I'm short of breath." The raccoon mother, panting, came to see Dr. Dinosaur. Dr. Dinosaur took out his stethoscope. "Okay, please breathe slowly." "Huff, huff, huff. Like this?" "No, not like that. Please breathe once every 3 seconds." 
3 seconds?

[P4] Dr. Dinosaur extended his arm to show the raccoon mom his watch. "You see, the thin, long hand—each 'tick-tock' movement is one second." The raccoon mom nodded. "Ah, now I understand."

Show children the second hand on the clock.
Let them see how the second hand moves and hear the sound it makes.

Tick-tock, tick-tock, tick-tock, breathe.
Tick-tock, tick-tock, tick-tock, breathe.
After three seconds of breathing, the raccoon mom, who had been feeling chest tightness, slowly felt better.

[P5] 2 PM
"Doctor, prescribe me some medicine!" "Doctor, give me an injection!" "My whole body hurts!" The dinosaur doctor was overwhelmed.
At that moment, the phone rang, "Ring ring, ring ring." It was Grandpa Rhinoceros from the village across the way. The dinosaur doctor picked up the phone and said, "I'm too busy right now, please call back in 1 minute."

[P6] "One minute?" asked Grandpa Rhino. "When the second hand goes around once, that's one minute. When the minute hand moves one notch, that's also one minute." "Ah, so if I count to 60 in my head, that's one minute, right?" "Of course! Even if you clap your hands 60 times, that's one minute too." "Haha, now I know what one minute is!" Grandpa Rhino happily hung up the phone.
Let children look at the minute hand on the clock. If they can directly see the second hand go around once while the minute hand moves one notch, the impression will be much deeper.

[P7] 4:00 PM
Dr. Dinosaur is treating a little bear with a tummy ache. "I've given you the shot, and you'll feel better soon. Remember to take your medicine 30 minutes after eating." "30 minutes after eating?" the little bear shakes his head, confused.

[P8] The dinosaur doctor shows the little bear his watch.
"If the minute hand turns half a circle, that's 30 minutes. Two 30-minute periods make one hour."

The little bear smiles and says, "If I finish eating at 6 o'clock, I should take my medicine at 6:30." "Yes, that's right," the dinosaur doctor smiles back.

One hour is 60 minutes.
So two 30-minute periods make one hour.

[P9] 7 PM
The stars are already twinkling. The dinosaur doctor begins changing clothes to go home.
"Hmm, it will take about 1 hour. I should be home around 8 o'clock."

[P10] "Dong dong dong! Dong dong dong!" At this moment, someone was knocking on the door. It was Ostrich Sister.
"Doctor, please help me. The dog mom seems to be giving birth to puppies!" The dinosaur doctor quickly opened the door. "Come in, come this way!"

[P11] While the dinosaur doctor is helping the dog mom, Ostrich Sister waits nervously beside. The second hand ticks and tocks, the minute hand moves one notch at a time, and the hour hand doesn't move at all. Time feels so slow.

[P12] 9 PM
"Congratulations, your cute baby is born!" Hearing the dinosaur doctor's words, the ostrich sister cried happily. "Dinosaur doctor, thank you so much!" "Hahaha, don't mention it."
The dinosaur doctor looked at his watch and smiled. He had had a fulfilling day, just like the watch hands that never stop.

Look at the clock in the picture and ask the child what time it is. Help the child calculate how long it took for the dog mom to give birth to her puppies.

[P13] Extension Exercise: Let's calculate time together.
It would be great if we could know how much time has passed without looking at a clock! Let's use my own clock to calculate time.
1 second
Close and open your eyes.
"Snap!"
Clap once.
1 minute
A healthy adult's heart beats "thump-thump" 60-100 times. You can also measure your friends' heartbeats for 1 minute.
Have a simple phone call with a friend.
1 hour
Watch an interesting TV program.
Draw a beautiful picture and color it in.

[P14] Tick-tock clock.
The shortest hand shows "hours"; one hour is 60 minutes.
The longest hand shows "minutes"; one minute is 60 seconds.
The thinnest hand shows "seconds".
The hands move in this direction.
Draw the hands on the clocks.
Where will the hands be after 30 minutes?
Where will the hands be after 1 hour?
Where will the hands be after 2 hours?
full_summary_zh:
[P1] 本页为绘本的封面，标题为《教你认认时分秒》，属于《我的第一本数学童话》系列，展示了作者、绘者、译者及出版社信息，画面中有恐龙、小猫和时钟等元素。
[P2] 本页介绍了恐龙先生是一位医术高明的医生，上午8点他匆忙赶往医院，画面中显示了医院、病人和他闪烁的手表。
[P3] 上午10点，浣熊妈妈因胸闷来找恐龙医生，医生指导她用3秒钟呼吸一次，浣熊妈妈对此感到困惑。
[P4] 恐龙医生向浣熊妈妈解释秒针的运作方式，通过‘滴答’声帮助她理解一秒的概念，并指导她用3秒钟呼一气，缓解胸闷症状。
[P5] 下午2点，恐龙医生在医院里忙得不可开交，许多病人要求开药或打针。这时，犀牛爷爷来电，恐龙医生请他1分钟后再次来电。
[P6] 恐龙医生通过电话向犀牛爷爷解释了1分钟的概念，用秒针转一圈、分针动一下、数到60或拍手60下等方法帮助其理解，犀牛爷爷听后高兴地挂了电话。画面下方有提示文字，建议让孩子观察钟表分针的移动以加深对时间的理解。
[P7] 下午4点，恐龙医生为肚子疼的小熊打完针后，叮嘱他饭后30分钟吃药，小熊对此感到困惑。
[P8] 恐龙医生向小熊解释30分钟和1小时的关系，通过手表分针转动半圈的概念帮助小熊理解，并确认饭后30分钟吃药的时间安排。
[P9] 晚上7点，恐龙医生准备下班回家，他换下工作服，并估算路上需要1小时，预计8点左右到家。
[P10] 夜晚，恐龙医生听到敲门声，原来是鸵鸟姐姐前来求助，称狗妈妈即将生产，恐龙医生立即开门迎接。
[P11] 恐龙医生正在为狗妈妈接生，鸵鸟姐姐在一旁焦急等待，画面通过钟表指针的缓慢移动，表现出等待时时间流逝的缓慢感。
[P12] 晚上9点，狗妈妈顺利生下小狗，鸵鸟姐姐激动落泪，恐龙医生感到欣慰，他回顾充实的一天，如同不停转动的表针。画面下方提示家长引导孩子观察钟表并计算接生所用时间。
[P13] 本页为拓展练习，通过图文结合的方式，引导孩子理解1秒钟、1分钟和1小时的具体时长，例如眼睛一闭一睁、拍一次手、心跳次数、通话、看电视或画画等活动，帮助孩子建立对时间的直观感受。
[P14] 本页通过图文结合的方式，介绍钟表的基本结构（时针、分针、秒针）及其功能，并设置练习题，引导孩子在钟表上画出30分钟、1小时和2小时后指针的位置，帮助建立对时间单位的直观理解。
